summary: Iter184 — Re-tested the Waybill button bug fix from iter183. BOTH backend & frontend verified end-to-end. Backend pytest 9/9 PASS (including the new test_public_waybill_query_param_token that exercises ?edit_token=... query-param fallback, header backward-compat, and garbage-token 401 rejection). Frontend Playwright: created shipment + PIN 9999 + 1 item; opened /donate/shipment/{token}; clicked 'Editor login' → entered PIN → editor badge appeared; clicked Waybill button [data-testid='ship-donor-waybill'] → popup tab opened with URL containing 'edit_token=' AND body showing the rendered HTML waybill ('Waybill / Manifest · Iter184 Waybill Test · 1 items · Total value: $10.00 · Total weight: 0.50 kg') — NOT a 401 JSON page. Bug is fully fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is clean: require_shipment_editor (shipments.py:117-119) reads X-Shipment-Edit-Token header first, then falls back to request.query_params['edit_token']. This is the standard pattern for header-gated endpoints that must also be reachable via window.open()/<a> links.
Frontend ShipmentDonorPage.jsx:260 properly URL-encodes the editToken via encodeURIComponent before appending. Good.

Security check verified: GET with neither header nor query param → 401; GET with ?edit_token=garbage → 401 (covered by test_public_waybill_query_param_token). No token leak risk beyond what the previous header-only design already had.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — Waybill popup opens with HTML content, edit_token query param present, no 401

rca of the issue: Already documented in iter183.
